title: Dart Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: main is where this Dart program starts. print shows a value.

examples.title: Keep a named number
examples.description: var lets Dart work out a type from a value. Numbers can be added with +.

examples.title: Keep a value fixed
examples.description: final means a name can be assigned only once. It helps protect a value from accidental changes.

examples.title: Build a text message
examples.description: A dollar sign places a variable inside a Dart string.

examples.title: Make a choice
examples.description: if checks a Boolean rule. The else branch runs when that rule is false.

examples.title: Add a list item
examples.description: A List keeps values in order. add places a new value at the end.

examples.title: Visit each item
examples.description: for-in reads each value of a list in order.

examples.title: Return a small result
examples.description: A function gives a calculation a name. The arrow form returns one expression.
examples.code:
int twice(int n) => n * 2;
void main() { print(twice(4)); }

examples.title: Use named keys
examples.description: A Map pairs keys and values. It can find a value by a text label.

examples.title: Choose a fallback
examples.description: String? can hold text or null. ?? chooses a fallback when the value is null.

examples.title: Make a small object
examples.description: A class is a plan for objects. Its constructor fills in the starting fields.

examples.title: Wait for a future value
examples.description: A Future represents a result that may arrive later. await reads that result inside an async function.
